1. (Currently Amended) A cell comprising: a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide __that is heterologous to the cell__.

2. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment is self-assembled in vivo __and the BMC polypeptide is expressed from a heterologous nucleic acid construct__.

3. (Original) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment further comprises at least one targeted enzyme.

4. (Original) The cell of claim 3 wherein the non-native compartment comprises a plurality of different targeted enzymes.

5. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 or claim 4 wherein the at least one targeted enzyme comprises a compartment-specific targeting signal sequence __and is heterologous to the cell__.

6. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the BMC polypeptide comprises a Eut polypeptide __and is heterologous to the cell__.

7. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 6 wherein the Eut polypeptide comprises a EutS polypeptide __and the EutS polypeptide is expressed from a heterologous nucleic acid construct__.

8. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the proteinaceous shell comprises a plurality of different BMC polypeptides __that are heterologous to the cell__.

9. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different bacterial species __and at least one of the BMC polypeptides is heterologous to the cell and expressed from a heterologous nucleic acid construct__.

10. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different BMC operons __and at least one of the BMC polypeptides is heterologous to the cell__.

11. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein at least one BMC polypeptide comprises an affinity tag __and the BMC polypeptide comprising the affinity tag is heterologous to the cell__.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: introducing into a host cell a polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide __that is heterologous to the host cell__, thereby producing a transformed cell; and growing the transformed cell under conditions effective for the transformed cell to express the polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and produce a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising the at least one BMC polypeptide __for the purpose of engineering a new metabolic capability in the host cell__.

13. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a bacterium __and the BMC polypeptide is from a different bacterial species than the host cell__.

14. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Enterobacteriaceae __and the BMC polypeptide is heterologous to the member of the family Enterobacteriaceae__.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 14 wherein the member of the family Enterobacteriaceae comprises E. coli __and the BMC polypeptide is from a non-E. coli source__.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Shewanellaceae __and the BMC polypeptide is heterologous to the member of the family Shewanellaceae__.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a yeast __and the BMC polypeptide is from a bacterial source heterologous to the yeast__.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17 wherein the yeast comprises a member of the family Saccharomycetaceae __and the BMC polypeptide is from a non-yeast source__.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 18 wherein the member of the family Saccharomycetaceae comprises Saccharomyces cerevisiae __and the BMC polypeptide is from a bacterial source__.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises an alga __and the BMC polypeptide is heterologous to the alga__.

21. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: providing a cell comprising a non-native compartment comprising: a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide __that is heterologous to the cell__, and at least one enzyme that catalyzes conversion of a substrate to a product __wherein the substrate and product are not naturally metabolized by the cell in the absence of the non-native compartment__; and growing the cell under conditions effective for the at least one enzyme to catalyze conversion of the substrate to a product.

22. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a bioactive product __not naturally produced by the cell__.

23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a drug or a drug precursor __not naturally produced by the cell__.

24. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a biofuel or a precursor of biofuel production __not naturally produced by the cell__.

25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the at least one enzyme catalyzes a step in degrading or detoxifying a toxic substrate __and the cell does not naturally degrade or detoxify the toxic substrate without the non-native compartment__.

26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 further comprising isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments __wherein the non-native compartments are isolated based on the presence of the heterologous BMC polypeptide__.

27. (Original) The method of claim 26 wherein at least a portion of the non-native compartment comprise an affinity tag and isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments comprises contacting a sample comprising the non-native compartments with an affinity substrate having selective affinity for the affinity tag.

28. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 comprising a plurality of compartments __wherein each compartment comprises at least one heterologous BMC polypeptide__.
